newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Alenia joins Envisat satellite.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Alenia joins Envisat satellite.

text.p: Italy's Alenia Spazio, a unit of state-owned Finmeccanica, said on Tuesday it had joined a German-run project to build Envisat, the biggest European satellite to date, to study the earth and the ozone layer.
Alenia said in a statement it had signed two contracts with Dasa-Dornier, the Daimler-Benz AG unit which is heading the project, worth some 100 billion lire ($65.5 million).
The Italian group will provide high-tech radar altimeter and microwave radiometer equipment intended to allow the satellite to study the sea with unprecedented accuracy.
Envisat, which will study the earth's surface, the seas and the atmosphere with particular attention to the ozone layer, is due for launch in 1999 and will have a life of five years.
As well as Dasa-Dornier and Alenia, France's Aerospatiale, Matra Marconi Space and some 80 other European and Canadian groups are collaborating on the project, which will cost around $1 billion.
